title: Cherry and almond tart
subtitle: sweet pastry filled with almond cream and fresh cherries baked until set
excerpt: Cherry and almond tart is a sweet pastry shell filled with almond frangipane and fresh, stoned cherries, baked until the cream has set around the fruit. The cherries sink slightly into the frangipane as they bake and release their juice into the filling. The tart cuts cleanly once cooled and keeps well for two days.
sourceNotes: The combination of cherries with almond cream has French and German origins. The Alsatian kirsch-based cherry tart and the French clafoutis are related preparations. Almond-and-cherry tarts became widely popular in British home baking during the late twentieth century.

glossaryTerms.definition: An almond-based cream made from butter, sugar, eggs, and ground almonds, used as a filling for tarts and pastries.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps at room temperature, loosely covered, for 2 days. The pastry softens slightly on the second day.

content.text: Cherry and almond tart is a sweet pastry case filled with

and fresh stoned cherries, baked until the almond cream sets around the fruit. The cherries release juice into the filling as they cook, so the frangipane comes out deep, moist, and faintly coloured. The pastry is partially blind-baked before filling to keep the base crisp.

Make the pastry: rub the cold butter into the flour and icing sugar until fine. Mix in the egg yolk and cold water until the dough just comes together. Chill for 30 minutes. Roll out, line a 23 cm tart tin, and chill for 15 minutes more.

Blind bake at 200 degrees C (fan 180 degrees C / gas 6) for 15 minutes with baking paper and beans. Remove the beans and paper and return to the oven for 5 minutes. The base should be set but not yet coloured. Reduce the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4).
Make the frangipane: beat the softened butter and caster sugar until light. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then fold in the ground almonds and vanilla.
Spread the frangipane into the warm pastry case. Press the stoned cherries into the surface in an even layer. Scatter flaked almonds over the top if using.
Bake at 180 degrees C for 30 to 35 minutes until the frangipane is set, golden, and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 30 minutes before unmoulding.

attrs.problem: Frangipane still liquid at the centre after the full baking time
attrs.avoid: Avoid checking too early; the filling needs the full time to set even though it looks done on top.
attrs.fix: A skewer inserted in the centre should come out clean, not wet. Cover the tart loosely with foil if the top is browning too fast and continue baking until the skewer is clean.

attrs.problem: Pastry shrinking away from the sides during blind baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid stretching the pastry when lining the tin; it springs back during baking.
attrs.fix: Press the pastry gently into the tin rather than pulling it to fit. Let it hang over the edge slightly and trim after blind baking.
